about.title: Woodside Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside sits along winding roads like Rt 84, Woodside Road, Portola Road, and La Honda Road, where residents drive, bike, and haul equipment for daily life on this semi-rural stretch of San Mateo County. Product problems here don't always announce themselves clearly — a bike component that snaps on a hill, a defective auto part that fails on a curve, a faulty piece of farm or ranch equipment, or a household appliance that malfunctions. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, just that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm — we connect people in Woodside with an independent attorney who can look at what happened and explain the options, without any upfront cost or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Woodside Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims under strict liability, meaning the focus stays on whether the product was defective, not on proving the maker was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may give you more than one avenue to pursue answers.

items.title: Free Connection, No Pressure
items.desc: LawProactive doesn't charge for connecting you with an independent attorney, and any attorney in the network typically works on contingency — no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often central evidence in a defect claim. An attorney can advise on safe storage while things are reviewed.

items.question: Does it matter that Woodside is a smaller, rural-feeling community?
items.answer: Not for the legal analysis — defect claims depend on the product and how it failed, not on the size of the town. That said, local details, like whether the product was used on winding roads such as La Honda Road or in home and ranch settings common in Woodside, can help paint a fuller picture of what happened.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability approach, you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless or aware of the problem. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation and explain what evidence may be relevant.
